title: Evaluating Existing-Building Green Rating Systems Through Heidegger’s Fourfold
content: Existing-building rating systems increasingly evaluate sustainability through automated performance telemetry, risking what Martin Heidegger termed technological enframing (Gestell). The objective of this study is to bridge Heidegger’s spatial phenomenology of the Fourfold (Das Geviert—Earth, Sky, Mortals, and Divinities) with empirical building assessment to evaluate how consecutive U.S. Green Building Council (USGBC) rating architectures operationalize—or distort—authentic dwelling (Wohnen). Credit structures for LEED-EB v4 (110 points), LEED-EB v4.1 (100 points), and LEED-EB v5 (110 points) were classified by quantitative performance (P) versus prescriptive (R) pathways and mapped onto the Fourfold, revealing an oscillation from v4’s procedural parity (54P/56R) to v4.1’s telemetry dominance (90P/10R) and v5’s decarbonization-led hybrid (85P/25R). Empirical benchmarking of eight USGBC-certified California Gold office buildings demonstrated that tier differentials inverted from Mortals-driven transit and daylighting in v4 (12-point gap) to Sky-driven energy telemetry in v4.1 (19-point gap), while projects across both cohorts scored zero points in rainwater management, site stewardship, sustainable purchasing, and grid harmonization. To restore reciprocal mirror-play (Spiegel-Spiel), this study introduces LEED-H O+M, a symmetrical 100-point rating system allocating 25 points to each Fourfold pole and embedding qualitative phenomenological Audit modules alongside quantitative verification.
